text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Unlikely that Russian President Boris Yeltsin's former security advisor Alexander Lebed, or anyone else, would have been seriously planning a military coup, says editorial.

- Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev offered Finnish President Urho Kekkonen political and economic support to keep left-centre coalition government of Prime Minister Mauno Koivisto in power at the end of the 1960s, Kekkonen's notes show. @

- All Nordic countries set to join Scengen treaty, which will create a border-free Europe, at end of 1998 or early 1999. Non-EU countries Norway and Iceland to sign cooperation agreement enabling them to take part.
- Greenpeace disrupted unloading of Finnish paper at German port of Lubeck. Environmentalists claimed paper was made of wood from ancient forests. Paper-maker Enso denies it.
- Left Wing Alliance party European Parliament candidate Esko Seppanen, who opposed linking markka to the ERM, tops poll with 10.7 percent support. @
- Opposition Centre Party threatens to bring parliamentary question on ERM link.
- Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs, on visit to Finland, says joining NATO only a matter of time for Finland.
- Forestry group UPM-Kymmene, biggest single owner of Finnyards, wants to get out of the ship-building business.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Forest industry again facing oversupply problems, likely to weigh down prices and mill utilisation rates, analyst says. @
- Finland's low rate of investment during recession years undermining chances of return to rapid growth, says economics professor.
- At worst, the losses from bankrupt Elake-Kansa pension insurance company could be 1.5 billion markka -- a bill other pension insurers and wage-earners would have to pay.
- Nokian Renkaat says it aims to increase sales by 50 percent over next five years. @
DEMARI
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says it is time for his Social Democratic Party to enter "active phase" on question of Finnish membership in European Economic and Monetary Union.
- Poll shows governing Social Democrats likely to win five of Finland's 16 European Parliament seats, up from current four, in Sunday's election.
AAMULEHTI
- Finland set to host NATO partnership for peace exercises for first time in 1998.
- Finnish limits on travellers' duty-free alcohol may be raised next year. @
